meaning:
δια-βλέπω
1. to took straight before one.
2. to see clearly: Mat.7:5, Mrk.8:25, Luk.6:42 (cf. διάβλεψις, Aq., Isa.61:1, for LXX ἀνάβ-).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.
Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own…
